newsitem.title: GERMANY: Three kidnap suspects appear in Frankfurt court.
newsitem.headline: Three kidnap suspects appear in Frankfurt court.

text.p: Police searched woods and fields for kidnapped multi-millionaire Jakub Fiszman on Thursday as three suspects appeared in a Frankfurt court.

But in spite of five arrests and the recovery of a four million mark ($2.6 million) ranson, a big search found no trace of the victim who was abducted on October 1 and may be locked alone in some cellar or buried in an concealed dungeon.
Police said they were still hoping that Fiszman was alive.
It was not clear whether the other two suspects would be released, prosecutor Rainer Schilling told reporters.
About 500 police with sniffer dogs combed the woods and fields in the Taunus area, 50 km (30 miles) from the German financial centre.
Police would not say whether the suspects were cooperating with their sweep. By late afternoon they had not found anything, but said they would scour the countryside until nighfall.

"We still hope the victim is alive," Ulrich Petri, a police spokesman at the scene, told journalists. He added that there were many cases in history of people who survived despite being locked away without provisions for many days.
Petri said the densely-wooded and sometimes steep terrain was very difficult to search. If they failed to find anything the area would be sealed off after dark and guarded by police.

Then the search would be resumed the next morning, Petri said. "When we came here this morning we were optimistic we would find something, but it's such a big area to cover and we have to be careful that we are thorough," Petri said.

Police sealed off several hectares (acres) of land and barred journalists and television camera crews from entering the area in case they destroyed clues pointing to the whereabouts of the 40-year-old businessman.
Helicopters hovered overhead and police divers were brought in to search ponds in a huge operation which started at dawn.
At midday officers emerged from a densely-wooded hill empty-handed. "The first part of the search is over and has ended without success," Petri said.
Three German men and two women regarded by police as their main suspects were arrested on Wednesday. The suspects are aged between 26 and 51 years.
Police say more people may have been involved.
The only sign of life from Fiszman since he was abducted outside his Frankfurt office has been a telephone call the next day to a woman friend to say he was being held in a cellar.
Fiszman's brother Georg paid a ransom of four million marks ($2.6 million) on October 10, but his kidnappers reneged on an agreement and failed to free him the following day.
German police recovered the ransom money on Wednesday in the garden of a flat in Wiesbaden. Two 1,000 mark notes were missing.
